archetype.name: Game Manager (short-area distributor)
archetype.definition: Bagent wins by staying on schedule: accurate throws underneath and over the middle inside Ben Johnson's structure, with the offense's play-calling and receivers supplying most of the explosiveness.

report.headline: Accurate, careful fill-in thriving in a good system; red zone is the problem.
report.take:
Tyson Bagent is filling in for Caleb Williams, and so far he has done it the way a backup should. In his one full game, 100% of snaps in the 23-12 win over the Jets, he went 25 of 34 for 268 yards and +7.9 passing EPA. His season CPOE of 7.99 ranks 3rd of 42, and his bad-throw rate of 2.3% is the lowest among charted qualifiers. He isn't pushing the ball. Intended air yards sit at 5.82 and he averages 1.7 yards short of the sticks on his throws. What he is doing is putting short and middle-of-the-field throws where his receivers can run with them. Throws over the middle are worth +0.494 EPA with an 80% success rate.

Much of this belongs to the setting. Chicago's offense ranks 8th in EPA and 6th in pass EPA, and the line allows a hit rate that ranks 5th. Bagent has been pressured on just 6.8% of dropbacks, the lowest rate in the sample. His 2023 season is the control group: -0.093 EPA per play, 6.01 YPA, -2.4 CPOE and 6 interceptions in 5 games. Those numbers were well below average. A 10-point CPOE swing on 43 attempts is partly real growth and comfort in a better scheme. It is also partly a clean pocket and a small sample. Note too that the team's start log credits Case Keenum with Weeks 3 and 4, which doesn't square with Bagent's 100% snap share in Week 4. His QB2 depth tag and that game are the best evidence of who runs the offense Sunday.

The numbers also hide some soft spots. He has zero touchdowns on 43 attempts (41st of 42 in TD rate). His 14 red-zone plays produced -0.307 EPA and a 28.6% success rate, so a well-run offense kept stalling short of the end zone. The 3-for-3 deep line (+1.736 EPA per play) is three throws, not a trait. Meanwhile intermediate throws have gone 6 of 13 with the interception, which is where tighter windows test him. Under center he's at -0.216 EPA, against +0.294 from shotgun. His legs add nothing: 4 carries for 1 yard and -0.964 EPA per carry.

Going forward, this is a short window. Williams's estimated return is October 18, so the Packers game is likely Bagent's last guaranteed start for now. In that window he gets a 24th-ranked pass defense, and Green Bay will be without Micah Parsons and Edgerrin Cooper. If he can turn red-zone trips into touchdowns, this run looks like a capable backup. If not, it looks like a nice game against the Jets.

strengths.title: Accuracy well above expectation
strengths.body: His CPOE of 7.99 ranks 3rd and his 2.3% bad-throw rate is the lowest charted. He has completed 72.2% of short throws and all 8 behind the line. The scheme creates easy completions, and he isn't wasting them. Given his 2023 CPOE of -2.4, expect some drift back, but the short-area precision fits how he's being used.

strengths.title: Middle of the field, third down
strengths.body: Throws over the middle return +0.494 EPA at an 80% success rate. On third down he has converted 54.5% at +0.618 EPA. The average distance there was 3.8 yards, though, so he has been working from manageable spots. Rome Odunze has been his most productive read at +1.059 EPA per target on 8 targets.

strengths.title: Protected and careful with the ball
strengths.body: He has been pressured on just 6.8% of dropbacks and has no fumbles lost. His sack rate of 4.4% ranks 11th. The 2023 version already avoided sacks well (pressure-to-sack rate ranked 4th), so ball security under duress is a carry-over trait, not a new one.

concerns.title: Red zone stalls, no touchdowns
concerns.body: He has 0 TDs on 43 attempts. His 14 red-zone plays went for -0.307 EPA at 28.6% success, with 6 of 13 completions and a sack. Compressed fields take away the short-area spacing he lives on, and he adds nothing as a runner to compensate. Some of this is small-sample bad luck, but it fits a passer who doesn't threaten tight windows.

concerns.title: Struggles once windows tighten
concerns.body: Intermediate throws are 6 of 13 (46.2%) with a -4.9 CPOE and his only interception. Under-center dropbacks run -0.216 EPA, against +0.294 from shotgun. Both point to a passer who is comfortable with defined reads and less so when he has to drive the ball or work play-action timing. His 2023 tape (-0.093 EPA per play) suggests this is the real ceiling.

concerns.title: Protection without Braxton Jones
concerns.body: Left tackle Braxton Jones (65% of snaps) is on IR until November. Bagent's spotless pressure numbers came mostly against the Jets. In the Week 2 relief stint against Minnesota he was pressured 30% of the time and produced -2.8 EPA. If the replacement tackle leaks, his accuracy edge shrinks fast.

trend.note: He went from a rough 9-attempt relief stint against the league's top defense (Minnesota, -2.8 EPA) to a full, efficient start against the Jets (+7.9 EPA). That is two games, with very different roles.

nextGame.headline: Depleted Packers defense suits his underneath game
nextGame.body:
Green Bay's defense ranks 26th in EPA, 24th against the pass and 24th in success rate. It also gives up +0.088 EPA on short throws (19th), which is exactly where Bagent works. The catch is that the Packers rank 4th in limiting explosive passes, so his yards will have to come in chunks of 6-12, not on shots. That is fine for his profile but caps the ceiling. They've also held QBs to 220 yards a game (6th fewest).

Availability tilts toward Chicago. Micah Parsons (ACL) is out and hasn't played this season. Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (83% of snaps) is lost for the year, which thins the middle of the field where Bagent has done his best work. Corner Brandon Cisse (90%) is questionable. On Chicago's side, Williams is out, and Bagent is listed questionable but practiced fully. Braxton Jones is on IR and running back Kyle Monangai (thumb) is day-to-day. Green Bay's offense is missing center Jacob Monk and guard Aaron Banks, with a tackle on IR, and it already allows the 2nd-highest hit rate. That makes it a bad matchup for a Bears defense ranked 4th in sack rate and 2nd in pass defense.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs. soft coverage underneath
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay ranks 19th against short throws and 24th in pass EPA. Bagent's short throws return +0.169 EPA with 61% success. Without Cooper, linebacker coverage over the middle should be weaker, so the Odunze and Burden crossers should be open.

keyMatchups.title: Bears pass rush vs. patched Packers line
keyMatchups.body: Chicago's defense ranks 2nd in pass EPA and 4th in sack rate. Green Bay's offense is 26th in EPA and dead last in rushing EPA, and it is down its starting center and a guard. A Bears defense controlling the game keeps Bagent in favorable scripts and limits how much he has to throw.

keyMatchups.title: Finishing in the red zone
keyMatchups.body: Bagent's red-zone success rate is 28.6%. Green Bay allows 1.5 passing TDs a game to QBs (10th fewest). Whether Chicago's drives end in touchdowns or field goals decides both his line and the margin.

nextGame.watch: Red-zone trips: whether Bagent can throw his first touchdown or the drives keep ending in field goals.

restOfSeason.body:
Williams's estimated return date is October 18, so Bagent's starting window may be just this week. After that he returns to a QB2 role with minimal production. As long as he starts, the short-area accuracy and low turnover risk look reasonably sustainable inside this offense. The CPOE near 8 and the perfect deep line should regress toward his weaker 2023 baseline. The zero-touchdown rate should also move up somewhat with more red-zone trips, because a top-8 offense will create them.

The projections below assume he is starting. If Williams returns on schedule, expect near-zero output, with Bagent mattering only if the hamstring lingers.
swingFactors: Left tackle play without Braxton Jones

bets.reason: Green Bay's offense ranks 26th in EPA and last in rushing EPA, and it is missing two interior linemen against a Bears defense ranked 5th overall and 2nd against the pass. Chicago leans run-heavy (passRateOverExp 23rd) with a red-zone-shy backup QB. Both Bagent games went under.

Chicago has the better unit on both sides of this matchup: offense 8th vs. a 26th-ranked defense, defense 5th vs. a 26th-ranked offense. Green Bay is also missing Parsons and Cooper. The backup-QB discount and red-zone stalls keep this from being stronger, since field goals make a 3-point margin fragile.

Green Bay allows the 4th-lowest explosive pass rate and just 220 QB yards per game, and Bagent doesn't push the ball (5.8 intended air yards). A script where Chicago's defense controls the game also trims attempts.

confidence.note: 43 attempts, one full start, likely a short starting window.
